recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | IEC hosts official Electoral Code of Conduct Signing ceremony
recentItems.description:
With just weeks to go before the 4 November local government elections, IEC Chairperson Mosotho Moepya says political parties and candidates must ensure the battle for votes remains peaceful, tolerant and free from intimidation. Parties and independent candidates are signing the Electoral Code of Conduct at the Gallagher Convention Centre in Midrand, formally committing themselves to the rules governing free and fair campaigning. 

Moepya says the code is crucial to ensuring that the 136 790 certified candidates are able to campaign and communicate their messages without fear of attacks, intimidation or violence. The legally binding code prohibits political intimidation and incitement to violence and protects the right of contestants to campaign freely.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: KwaMakhutha Shooting | Police launch manhunt after 11 people were shot and killed
recentItems.description:
Police in KwaZulu-Natal have launched a manhunt for suspects who allegedly shot and killed eleven people and injured three others, during a shooting incident which happened at the Ziko area in KwaMakhutha last night. Information available at this stage suggests that thirteen men and one woman, who is believed to be pregnant, were reportedly having a party inside a house, when three men arrived and opened fire on them. 
Let's bring in SABC News Reporter, Nonhlakanipho Magwaza for more.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | IEC hosts official Electoral Code of Conduct Signing Ceremony for 2026 LGE
recentItems.description:
Political parties and independent candidates contesting the 2026 local government elections will commit to promoting conditions conducive to a free and fair poll. This as the IEC hosts a ceremony at Gallager Convention Centre, north of Johannesburg, where the contestants will pledge to campaigning with tolerance, allowing for open debate and rejecting violence and intimidation.
